doc.title: Derek Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: Working with singers and keys
summary: Smith talks about singers' keys and respect for those who know their keys.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Well, you know, it’s another skill. I used to get upset if singers would say that. Singers would come in with some sheet and say, “I do it in A” or “G flat” and you know, and I’d get real smart and say, “well I don’t.” But depending on how much respect you had for © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-
them. If it was some singer that I, you know, say oh she couldn’t tell the difference between the G flat and G, so I’m going to play it in the key that seems right for me.
Yeah, it’s in your key now, right?
But some of them know, and they’ll get my respect, and I’ll work with them.
Yeah. Working with singers can be very interesting.
You know they tell this joke they say, how do you know when there’s a singer on your front porch?
